title: The line the paper looks for
intro: This level takes the definition apart. It covers what the five properties were in the human literature before they became tests, what global workspace theory asserts beyond the idea of a shared store, why a transformer might or might not build one, and how the paper picked its candidate set before scoring it against the definition.

chapters.title: Five marks, turned into tests
chapters.body:
The list does not begin with the model. It begins with the properties the human literature attributes to consciously accessible information, and there are five of them. Such information is reportable: it can be put into words on request, and verbal report has often served as a primary empirical signature of [[access-consciousness]]. It is subject to top-down control, in that a concept can be deliberately summoned, held in mind and dismissed. It is the medium of deliberate reasoning, the effortful chaining of one step to the next. It permits flexible use: the same content can be routed to whatever operation the moment demands and recombined with other accessible content. And it is selective, since the bulk of perceptual, motor and linguistic work proceeds as [[unconscious-processing]], with none of this involved.

The contrast case the literature leans on is [[blindsight]]: visual information steers a patient's behavior while the patient reports having seen nothing.

[[fig-1]] restates each mark as something a set of vectors inside a model must do, and each restatement asks for an intervention rather than a correlation. For [[verbal-report]] it is not enough that the model names a concept the set holds. Exchanging one active vector for another, an operation the paper calls the [[lens-coordinate-swap]], has to change the answer.

[[directed-modulation]] asks the model to load the set on instruction while its visible output says nothing about the loaded content. [[internal-reasoning]] asks the set to carry the value of an unspoken intermediate step, and asks that editing that value redirect the conclusion. [[flexible-generalization]] asks that one vector, lifted from the context it arose in, be operated on correctly by whatever function the new context supplies.

[[selectivity]] is the one mark that can fail by the set proving too useful. The set has to be small, and it has to be unnecessary for routine parsing and fluent continuation.

All five have to hold. The label [[workspace-like-properties]] is a conjunction, not a menu.

chapters.title: What the theory asserts, past the shared store
chapters.body:
[[global-workspace-theory]] says more than that some store is shared. It supplies machinery, and the machinery is what makes it usable as a source of predictions.

The brain, on this account, is composed of many [[specialized-processors]] running in parallel and largely in isolation. Their activity proceeds outside conscious access. A representation becomes accessible when it is posted to the workspace and read by many of those processors at once, an act the theory calls [[global-broadcast]]. Broadcast carries a format requirement with it: the representation has to arrive in a code the processors share, or they could not read it. The workspace is described as a hub that integrates as well as distributes.

Two further commitments matter for what the paper goes looking for. The first is the [[workspace-capacity-limit]]. The workspace holds only a small selection of ongoing activity, so entry is competitive and open to attentional modulation. The second is [[ignition]]: entry is not gradual but a sharp, nonlinear transition from local to global availability.

Each of these is a thing to look for over and above the five functional marks. That is the paper's stated reason for adopting this theory rather than another. It grounds the functional properties in architectural and computational features, so it hands the investigation more than a checklist.

The adoption comes with a disclaimer, made in the same paragraph. The paper records that the global workspace model is not universally accepted, and that other accounts explain conscious access in different ways. Those alternatives, gathered later under [[theories-of-consciousness]], are left for the discussion. The theory is used as a comparison point, not as settled ground.

chapters.title: Reasons to expect one, and reasons not to
chapters.body:
The paper states the case against before the case for. In the brain the workspace is bound up with recurrent dynamics and with interactions between regions, and neither has a direct analog in a [[transformer]]. There are no obviously separable input processors to compete for entry. Whatever broadcast a language model performs happens inside a single feedforward pass, rather than through loops that carry a representation back to where it came from. The paper also allows that although it does observe some competition for entry, it cannot say whether that competition resembles the sharp ignition of the brain case.

The case for is an argument about usefulness rather than resemblance. A common representational format lets an intermediate result be written once and read by many processes. A model that has to chain reasoning steps, apply a general operation in whatever context it is handed, and answer questions about its own processing stands to benefit from that arrangement. Read this way, [[llm-global-workspace-hypothesis]] is not a claim about architecture. It is a claim about what a system under those pressures ends up organizing.

The distinction matters because nothing in the architecture supplies a workspace module. Earlier proposals did build one in: the consciousness prior and shared-workspace transformers add a workspace-like bottleneck by design, which the paper groups as [[workspace-inspired-architectures]]. A separate line of theoretical work derived [[indicator-properties]] from several theories of consciousness and asked whether current architectures could satisfy them in principle. This paper measures production models where nothing of the kind was imposed, so anything it finds is [[emergent-rather-than-designed-workspace]], a structure that appeared under ordinary [[next-token-prediction]] pressure.

One softening of the architectural gap is stated later in the paper but bears on the premise. A feedforward stack can reproduce a recurrent computation for a number of steps equal to its depth ([[feedforward-emulation-of-recurrence]]). Past that depth the model's only recourse is to write intermediate results into the context as tokens and read them back.

chapters.title: Choosing the candidates before scoring them
chapters.body:
A model's repertoire is large and mixed. The paper lists what earlier interpretability work has already read out of activations: the part of speech of the current word, the length in characters of a line of text, entities such as the Golden Gate Bridge, psychological states such as desperation, and situational knowledge such as being under evaluation. If a workspace exists, some of these belong to it and most do not. Selecting the subset is the first problem, and it has to be settled before any test can be run.

The paper settles it using property one alone. A [[verbalizable-representation]] is one poised to be put into words should the occasion arise. That is not the same as a direction that happens to be verbalized in the context at hand. The separation is made by averaging across a large corpus of contexts instead of reading one: a direction that disposes the model toward a word across contexts counts, while a direction that leads to the word here may be nothing but this context's business. The instrument that performs the averaging is the [[jacobian-lens]], and its vectors span the [[j-space]].

Two limits are declared at this point. The lens yields one direction per entry in the [[tokenizer-vocabulary]], so the concepts it can name are exactly those with single-token names ([[single-token-limitation]]). And the whole construction rests on the working assumption of the [[linear-representation-hypothesis]], that concepts are directions and activations are sums of them.

Selecting on verbalizability also builds in an agreement the paper is careful not to cash. Because the lens is derived from the average effect of activations on output tokens, some match between what it reads and what the model then says is expected by construction ([[report-relation-by-construction]]). The report result cannot rest on that match. It rests on the swap changing the answer.

The search order is what gives the rest its force. Four of the five properties played no part in choosing the set, and the paper reports that the set satisfied them anyway, calling that outcome surprising. [[theme-the-workspace-claim]] is the definition; everything after it is the scoring.
